Data.application_name: Roads of Da Vinci: In Search of Origins
Data.application_name_se: Roads of Da Vinci: In Search of Origins Collector's Edition
Data.Cutscene001Page001Start01: So today’s lecture is about the origins of Roman mythology. And yes — its roots lie in Greece.
Data.Cutscene001Page001Start02: Their world was ruled by gods. And above all of them — Jupiter.
Data.Cutscene001Page001Start04: Legio, ad pugnam! Celeriter ad victoriam! (Legion, to battle! Swiftly to victory!)
Data.Cutscene001Page001Start07: The people worshipped soil and rain — not just a god with thunder.
Data.Cutscene001Page001Start08: Shall we prove it in the field?
Data.Cutscene001Page001Start10: Perfetto! Whoever finds more evidence — wins.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start01: Helmet — check, spear — check, shield — in place...
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start02: Weapons, armor, stance, build, even the way they “stood and scared the world” matched between Ares and Mars almost too perfectly.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start03: The differences, as in life and science, lay not in looks, but in the meaning behind them.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start04: Ares was not loved by the Greeks: feared, despised, endured as an evil necessity.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start05: Mars, however, was a public favorite, a pillar of Rome and its official patron.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start06: In truth, it was the same warrior image, moved into a new value system.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start07: I studied the relics with that feeling when intuition knows, but reason still pretends to doubt.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start08: The conclusion was simple: Rome borrowed the image, changed the context, added a label.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start09: Rome created no new god, but masterfully reinterpreted an old one.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start10: The puzzle clicked! Not because images matched, but because image is not meaning — and that shaped my theory.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start11: Still, this is not enough to triumphantly wave proof at Leonardo.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start12: If Rome turned Ares into Mars, they likely did the same with others.
Data.Cutscene002Page001Start13: Not in the city center, but beyond it... Diana is the perfect candidate!
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start01: For some time, we had been studying the relics we found, along with those brought by colleagues who worked with Greek cults.
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start02: Andrew suddenly grabbed Artemis’s bow and aimed an arrow at me: “What do you have to say in your defense, goddess who looks like me?!”
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start03: Without hesitation, I raised Diana’s bow and stepped forward, joining the game.
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start04: “We may share a face, Artemis, but our eyes look in different directions,” I replied.
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start05: “My groves are not for humans,” Andrew declared, “who come with noise, break branches, and demand what is not theirs!”
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start06: “People must not be driven away, but restrained from destruction, or the world’s balance will be lost,” I said softly.
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start07: “You let mortals come too close,” he shot back, “nature is stronger without them!”
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start08: “Nature is always strong. I am only her shield, not a wall that shuts everyone out,” I kept a straight face.
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start09: Andrew lowered the bow first and quietly chuckled in his own voice.
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start10: “So, sis, does that mean you hold all the arguments against Leonardo’s theory?”
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start11: “Yep,” I nodded, carefully returning the artifact, “now it’s his move.”
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start12: At that moment, I felt rare, almost childlike joy as a researcher.
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start13: Artemis embodies wild nature, which you cannot stare at or question freely.
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start14: Diana is nature itself, standing guard over the human world.
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start15: In that difference lies the second proof of how Rome borrowed gods and gave them new meaning.
Data.Cutscene003Page001Start16: All that remained was to wait for Leonardo’s countermove.
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start01: Claire kindly told me about her diary, and I solemnly vowed to keep my own notebook of great archaeological feats, to hand it to her one day.
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start02: The Professor taught me the basics of archaeology and, ovviamente (of course), as a descendant of Leonardo da Vinci, I grasped it all at once.
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start03: So my first entry is for an obvious fact: I already know where we’re heading next.
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start04: Etna. All the answers will be there.
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start05: Before the road to the volcano, we stopped in the nearest town for tea—purely out of scientific curiosity.
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start06: I’ve heard much about the local cuisine, but, davvero (truly), that’s a topic for a far more personal diary!
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start07: “Professore Bromwell, I’ve been to Etna,” I said aloud. “Don’t worry—I know this kind of terrain.”
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start08: “Commendable, Giuliano,” he smiled. “That will speed up our work.”
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start09: I suddenly noted, con una certa nostalgia (with a certain nostalgia), that my first name already sounded unfamiliar to me.
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start10: “Please, keep calling me by my second name—legends are easier to believe that way!” I said, not without pleasure.
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start11: “Giuliano Leonardo Alberti… a fine name for da Vinci’s descendant,” the professor mused. “As I understand it, all sources say he had no children.”
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start12: “In our family, the legend passed from generation to generation,” I replied calmly. “Davvero (truly), even great geniuses sometimes want to believe in a small miracle!”
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start13: “Fair point,” the professor looked at me with new interest.
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start14: “By the way,” I went on, “do you also think Vulcan could have been worshipped here as a living deity?”
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start15: “Hmm… you got ahead of my conclusion,” he admitted, mildly surprised.
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start16: “Genio riconosce genio (genius recognizes genius),” I allowed myself a smile.
Data.Cutscene004Page001Start17: For me, it was the moment to prove that the name da Vinci demands more than mere doubt.
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start01: The Professor and Andrew went ahead; Claire and I stayed on Etna, and I knew at once it was a momento storico (historic moment).
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start02: Time was disastrously short, but mamma mia (my God), have such trifles ever stopped a true researcher?
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start03: “Vulcan is a threat—worship him, bring gifts, or he’ll burn the city,” I read. “A stunning find! This is…”
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start04: “This is very dangerous!” Claire grabbed my cloak and hauled me toward the exit.
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start05: “Ovviamente (of course), if Vulcan existed, he’d be insulted by no gifts,” I grinned. “The ancients would adore that audacity.”
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start06: “No, they’d be terrified of the elements!” Claire insisted. “We must run, not debate what isn’t there!”
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start07: “Don’t worry, mia cara (my dear), the forecast says nothing bad will happen,” I said. “Otherwise they wouldn’t let us in.”
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start08: “Either way, the proof for my theory is already in my pocket,” I added, pleased.
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start09: “From what I know, Vulcan was modeled on Hephaestus—also borrowed—so I’m right!” Claire shot back.
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start10: “Not at all,” I perked up. “We found ties to fires, lightning, ruin, and bans on putting out the sacred flame…”
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start11: “Vulcan copies Hephaestus in looks, not essence: the smith yields to fire itself. Form matches; meaning doesn’t,” she said.
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start12: “Greek influence didn’t create a fire cult; it laid a Greek smith’s image over an older fire god!” I retorted.
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start13: “Fine,” Claire breathed, finally letting go. “We’ll discuss it later—when we get out alive.”
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start14: I call it an unquestionable success, magnifico (magnificent).
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start15: The first stone for my theory is thrown—and thankfully not at me.
Data.Cutscene005Page001Start16: Next on the plan… Janus, so it’s time to look both ways.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final01: Fresh air after long hours in cave dust was a true delight, and for the first time that day I let myself smile.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final02: Leonardo solemnly handed me his diary, and I skimmed the notes before he, of course, couldn’t hold back and spoke.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final03: “So, Janus is the key figure in my proof,” he declared, as if adding the final stroke to a fresco.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final04: “He existed before the Greeks arrived,” Leonardo went on, “and that says a lot about who came first.”
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final05: “But I haven’t been idle either,” I objected, closing the diary. “Mars, Diana, and Vulcan match Greek gods in looks, yet Rome reworked their essence.”
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final06: “Please, cara mia (my dear), what ‘reworking’!” Leonardo pressed, heated. “Rome had its own cult. They simply liked Greek images and dressed their gods in them!”
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final07: I froze, and in that moment all the fragments suddenly snapped into a single picture.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final08: “Leonardo… turns out we’re both right,” I said, feeling that rare, almost physical jolt of discovery. “We’re just talking about different eras of the gods’ lives!”
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final09: “Logico (logical),” he smiled, as if he’d been waiting for those words. “I described the gods before the Greeks; you—after they appeared.”
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final10: “Then let’s celebrate our shared victory—the victory of science!” I cheered. “By the way, what will you do next? Go back to the museum?”
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final11: “Domanda difficile (tough question),” he drawled, and for the first time truly thought it through.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final12: “I’ll talk to the Professor. He wanted to expand the team, and your inventions are a perfect calling card,” I added, winking.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final13: “Then I’m in. And now… La vittoria va celebrata (victory must be celebrated). My treat,” he bowed theatrically.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final14: “Deal!” I replied—and I meant it with all my heart.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final15: We walked on, arguing again, laughing, and discussing finds, as if everything before this hadn’t happened to us.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final16: Every story is unique, and every theory deserves a chance to be heard.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final17: Even a small contribution can push history forward—toward the world we dream of.
Data.Cutscene006Page001Final18: So I, Claire, swear to become an archaeologist who will strengthen the progress of her era!
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start01: “We’re not going any farther—the bus broke down,” the driver told our group matter-of-factly, then went off to fix it.
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start02: Leonardo instantly perked up, taking the breakdown as a challenge, and eagerly offered to upgrade the bus with his inventions.
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start03: A minute later he had already volunteered himself as the driver’s helper, glowing as if this were his first opera scene.
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start04: Sleepy Andrew noticed nothing, so we chose not to disturb him and left our brother in blissful ignorance.
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start05: The Professor and I stepped into the fresh air of an Italian village, and I stretched with pleasure, ready to suggest a short break.
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start06: “Since we have a moment, we can discuss the details of the upcoming expedition,” the Professor said, already opening his notes.
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start07: I yawned: “The archive is still a long way off. Leonardo is sure we’ll find traces of the places we studied last time.”
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start08: “What are you arguing about this time?” the Professor asked out of habit, without even looking up.
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start09: I smiled and reminded him that, while tracing Rome’s mythic roots, we ended up talking about Ceres and Faunus.
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start10: “Back then we waved the idea away,” I went on, “and now we’ve decided to return to it.”
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start11: I explained that rumors say the local archive mentions “six gifts of the earth” tied to ancient cults.
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start12: “If it all fits, we mustn’t waste a minute!” the Professor brightened…
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start13: …then we helplessly watched the repairs and exchanged a look.
Data.Cutscene007Page001Start14: A bad start to an expedition is a promise of a good ending, right?
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final01: The hillsides around us slowly sank into sunset light, and I felt that rare sense of completion finally catching up with us all.
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final02: “…And this puzzle turns out to be the last. Finalmente (at last), done,” Leonardo said, brimming with excitement.
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final03: “The evidence board is assembled; it’s time to return to camp and recheck everything,” the Professor said, eyes tired toward the tents.
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final04: “Yes, genius of the past, let’s wrap up,” I smiled at Leonardo. “Long hours of theory await us.”
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final05: “Ovviamente (obviously), we already have the proof,” he replied, unrolling a scroll fragment. “These six gifts were mentioned at least two millennia ago.”
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final06: “Fertility gods were honored above the rest,” the Professor began. “Farming and pasturelands were Rome’s economy; families and the state depended on them.”
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final07: “Logico (logical),” Leonardo nodded. “The ‘six gifts of the earth’ aren’t mere artifacts—they prove fertility’s priority.”
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final08: “Fertility gods were revered not for the biggest temples, but because their gifts were everywhere: homes, fields, roads, wells,” he added.
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final09: “One conclusion! This expedition could go on forever—our work will never truly end!” I laughed.
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final10: “And still… let’s finish,” Andrew yawned. “Time to call on the fertility gods and finally eat.”
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final11: The expedition ended, and fatigue gave way to quiet joy: we reached our goal!
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final12: Each answer only opens new questions, and ancient history, it turns out, has no final page.
Data.Cutscene008Page001Final13: If the road to truth is endless, then more great discoveries still await us.
Data.StartLvl01: On the way to the Colosseum, we decided I’d start hunting for proof. Leonardo will stay an observer for now—let him learn and soak up experience.
Data.StartLvl02: Disaster! Tourists packed everything around us, as if this were a festival, not a dig. We must quickly figure out how to clear a path for science.
Data.StartLvl03: Andrew pulled out a projector and announced a show. I wanted to calmly rebuild the past, but an eye-catching reenactment will do, too.
Data.StartLvl04: Clearly, we're short on tools. Archaeology leaves no room for improvisation, so let's restock our arsenal!
Data.StartLvl05: A local actor heard our talk about Mars’s past and claimed we’d got it all wrong. Now he’s leading us to the theater to show “how it really was.”
Data.StartLvl07: Back to the battlefield… I mean, the excavation. We learned a time capsule exists—and we need it!
Data.StartLvl08: Andrew overlaid ancient and modern maps of the Colosseum. The differences show, so old passages still exist—we just have to find them.
Data.StartLvl09: Nooo! We dropped a level down! And we hadn’t finished up there… but down here the finds promise to be far older—and far more exciting!
Data.StartLvl10: During the evacuation Andrew clipped a pipeline, and water started rising! Stay calm, Claire: first we save the dig, then we panic!
Data.StartLvl11: After the flood we found a hidden, previously unreachable part of the hypogeum. I can feel it—the answer to whose mythology came first is hiding here!
Data.StartLvl12: Mountains stood between us and Diana’s sacred grove. The route is tough, but the descents looked solid. I hope the goddess favors us today.
Data.StartLvl13: Leonardo’s invention beeped confidently: somewhere here a crucial artifact was hidden. I love mornings that start with a clear “it’s definitely here.”
Data.StartLvl14: We met another team of archaeologists. They needed help with scattered fragments of an artifact, and of course we volunteered.
Data.StartLvl15: Who was in charge of the pass?! Doesn’t matter now—the pass is lost. Without it, the sealed part of the grove is unreachable, so we search.
Data.StartLvl16: By my calculations and what we’ve found, the artifact is underwater!
Data.StartLvl17: This artifact is enormous! Looks like we won’t pull it from the water without some extra capabilities.
Data.StartLvl18: After an epic swim, we chose to rest and refill supplies. Rest is underrated—but vital—on any expedition.
Data.StartLvl19: The tracks led to a fresh landslide and a washed-out trail. We’ll have to clear the way, or we won’t reach the artifact.
Data.StartLvl21: At night someone prowled the grove. The “Diana = Artemis” proof vanished. More questions than answers… Who could have needed it?!
Data.StartLvl22: One colleague fell into a well during the dig. We must help fast, or the expedition could end right here.
Data.StartLvl23: All clues pointed to one spot. We found where Diana’s statue should be. The simplest part remains—getting it.
Data.StartLvl24: Ecco (just like that) Claire handed me command of the expedition. Now I set the course, and, modestamente (modestly speaking), it’s the right choice.
Data.StartLvl25: Prima di tutto (first of all), we must prove offerings were made out of fear of fire. Etna still holds traces of gifts that confirm it.
Data.StartLvl26: Che rumore è questo (what’s that noise)? Claire shouted about a collapse. Careful!
Data.StartLvl27: A quanto pare (it seems), we found the fissure where offerings were stored. If the theory’s right, this is where fire demanded tribute.
Data.StartLvl29: Purtroppo (unfortunately), our flashlights drown in steam and ash. Until we deal with it, we can’t go on.
Data.StartLvl30: Con rispetto (with respect) for local traditions, we chose to rest in town. Hot dogs gave way to farm-fresh meals at Claire’s insistence.
Data.StartLvl31: Ovviamente (of course), the meteorologists’ broken website didn’t stop us. We visited the station ourselves and checked the maps...
Data.StartLvl32: We’re back on Etna. The locals’ legends of Vulcan can wait—we must cross a zone of shifting gases.
Data.StartLvl34: Finalmente (at last), we found Vulcan’s sanctuary. Where else but here can I prove my theory about the birth of mythology?
Data.StartLvl35: Straordinario (extraordinary)! Right by the ruins, colleagues met us with news of discovered gates. Fate is clearly hurrying us along.
Data.StartLvl36: The gates stood before us—too perfect. Truth is rarely that smooth. Something about them feels off; we’ll verify they’re genuine.
Data.StartLvl38: Delusione (disappointment). The illusion crumbled—the gate was false. Even a genius needs a pause, so we retreated to regain our strength.
Data.StartLvl39: Caos (chaos). Power is out across the whole area. Claire insists we help restore communications, or the expedition will stall.
Data.StartLvl40: The route is unstable, but doubt isn’t an argument. Between the slopes, ne sono certo (I’m sure), the answer is hidden.
Data.StartLvl41: Imprevisto (unexpected)! We tumbled down—gracefully, of course. Luckily my drone caught a signal—there’s something here.
Data.StartLvl42: A new artifact changed the rules of the game. Torniamo (let’s return) to the dig and play the next round differently.
Data.StartLvl43: Attento (careful)! We didn’t fall—we tactically went deeper. The ground is unstable; move slowly, or we won’t reach the answers.
Data.StartLvl44: The professor noticed from afar: several pieces of one artifact lie around. We’ll join them and, sono convinto (I’m convinced), the hidden meaning will appear.
Data.StartLvl45: Destino (destiny). These aren’t scraps—these are Janus’s real gates. We’re close to proof that will change the debate. Now we must bring them up.
Data.StartLvl46: We made it! It’s breathtaking—these hills seem to breathe history. But awe can wait: first we map the motifs and put everything in its place.
Data.StartLvl47: By our calculations, the first of the “six gifts of the earth” is hidden right here. I can feel we’re on the brink of discovery.
Data.StartLvl48: Locals told a tale of a “ritual bull.” The description matches the gifts of the earth too precisely to be coincidence.
Data.StartLvl49: The path to the third gift, of course, came with a puzzle. Seems the ancients weren’t big on trust.
Data.StartLvl50: Journalists were debating an ancient goat imprint. If it’s tied to Faunus, we may be looking at one of the gifts of the earth.
Data.StartLvl51: The dawn sign “demands time.” We must crack its meaning, and then we’ll know where to seek the next gift of the earth.
Data.StartLvl52: The map led to private vineyards. Now comes the hardest part—convincing the farmer we come in peace, and for science.
Data.StartLvl53: Time is short and the task is tough. But if the artifact is here, we must act fast—and carefully!
Data.StartLvl54: The ancient text was stubborn: each of us translated it differently. We must solve it on site, or we won’t move forward.
Data.StartLvl55: Rumors swirl about a mysterious artifact at the festival. We must check whether a gift of the earth is disguised among the decorations.
Data.StartLvl56: We arrived at the harvest festival, and the Cup of Liber itself is in a display case! Now we must confirm its mythological meaning.
Data.StartLvl57: All six gifts are ours. Now we gather the evidence into one system—and present the results of our expedition.
Data.artifact_description01: Maps, scrolls, and a statue of Mars suggest he was invoked as a patron of battle. Whether this was faith or ritualized spectacle can no longer be clearly told.
Data.artifact_description02: Fragments of Diana rose from the ground as if the grove itself returned the goddess. Legends say she never left Nemi, only hid until the right moment.
Data.artifact_description03: Vessels, vows, and warnings carved in stone agree on one thing: fire was feared here. Altars of Vulcan stood far from people, not for worship, but for pleas of mercy.
Data.artifact_description04: False and true gates, a bell, and gathered fragments point to Janus as guardian of transitions. By legend, his gates opened in war and closed in times of peace.
Data.artifact_description05: Altars of bread, wine, sun, and hoofprints—little remains of the earth gods. Their names faded, yet harvests came, as long as they were remembered.
Data.trophies_description01: They say in early Rome Mars was honored not only for war. He guarded fields and order, and legions raised altars in camps, believing discipline mattered more than fury.
Data.trophies_description02: Diana was one of the few goddesses worshipped in Rome before Greek influence. Her cult knew little bloodshed and favored silence over spectacle.
Data.trophies_description03: Vulcan was not asked for help — he was begged not to rage. Fire was seen as living and dangerous, and altars stood far from cities, out of fear of being heard.
Data.trophies_description04: Janus is a purely Roman god, with no Greek counterpart. He was invoked first in every rite, for without a beginning there is no path. His gates opened in war and closed in peace.
Data.trophies_description05: The fertility gods were rarely written about. They were remembered when grain rose and wine matured. In fields and by hearths, people sang and believed: as long as the land is generous, Rome lives.

Data.Epic_Text_lvl07: The capsule's lock has rusted shut. Andrew suggests pouring soda over it. Sounds strange, but it's worth a try!
Data.Epic_Text_lvl08: Let's build a model of the Colosseum out of blocks to recreate its former appearance and find the secret passages.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl09: The door will only open for four lions, but one is missing. We'll have to come up with a convincing replacement!
Data.Epic_Text_lvl10: We need to find the old drain and direct the water toward it before the entire hypogeum floods!
Data.Epic_Text_lvl11: We need to examine the statue and get out of here, but the exit is blocked. Maybe the old catapult can help us escape?
Data.Epic_Text_lvl12_1: The elevator hasn't worked in ages, and there's no way down on foot. We'll have to figure out what's wrong with it and try to bring it back to life.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl12_2: The goats have blocked the way down and clearly aren't going to help us for free. Maybe a little treat will persuade them to do what we need.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl13: The windmill hasn't worked in years, so the artifact won't budge. We need to find the problem and fix it.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl14: The stones conceal an ancient puzzle, and to solve it we'll have to make some dynamite and blow them all up!
Data.Epic_Text_lvl15: We can't go any farther without a special pass. Maybe we'll find something in the old grottos that can help us solve this problem.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl16: The siphon is broken, and without it the water won't rise high enough. If we can repair it, perhaps the water itself will help us reach the artifact.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl17: It looks like the local water creatures can lift the artifact from the bottom. We just need to earn their trust and convince them to work together.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl18: After everything that's happened today, we could definitely use a break. And this dance machine looks like the perfect way to unwind!
Data.Epic_Text_lvl19: A whole mountain of sand is blocking the way ahead. We certainly can't clear it by hand... But if we repair this old vacuum cleaner, we might have a chance.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl21: That sneaky raccoon stole our pass and has no intention of giving it back! I wonder if a flirty raccoon doll could distract him long enough?
Data.Epic_Text_lvl22: An archaeologist is stuck in the well and can't get out on his own. But there are plenty of parrots nearby... Maybe we can recruit them for the rescue operation.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl23: A real artifact is hidden among these tourist statues, but there's no way to tell which one by sight. Looks like we'll have to get the entire collection and sort it out later.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl24: There are several roads ahead and not a single clue which one to take. Well, we'll have to check them one by one and find the right path ourselves.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl25: A valuable artifact is buried underground beneath layers of dirt and dust. We'll have to grab a broom and clear it layer by layer.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl26: The exit is blocked, and there's no normal way out anymore. But we do have an idea involving a battle top... It's crazy, of course, but why not try it?
Data.Epic_Text_lvl27: Apparently, the volcano isn't going to give up the artifact without a fight. If the ancient legends are true, we'll first have to prepare a worthy offering.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl29: The passage is completely filled with smoke – we can't see a step ahead. Maybe if we spray it with enough water, the smoke will settle and reveal the way?
Data.Epic_Text_lvl30: This weed is rooted firmly in the ground. But the wind is strong today... If we tie a kite to the plant, nature itself might do all the hard work for us.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl31: The station has lost power, and there's a thunderstorm raging nearby. Risky, but a properly positioned antenna might catch a bolt of lightning for us!
Data.Epic_Text_lvl32_1: We've found an ancient artifact, but I still don't understand its origin or purpose. We need to study it carefully – perhaps it will answer at least some of our questions.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl32_2: The volcano is constantly shrouded in smoke and ash, and it's surprisingly easy to lose your way here. We should leave some good signposts – they might save another researcher someday.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl34: A huge root is completely blocking the road. There's no way we can pull it out... But if we can get hold of a flamethrower, the problem might disappear along with the root.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl35: The other expedition clearly knows something they aren't eager to share. We'll have to come up with a good disguise and find out everything ourselves.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl36: Ancient gates stand before us... or at least they're trying very hard to look ancient. Before jumping to conclusions, we should check whether they're genuine.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl38: The kitten stole a hot dog and is now guarding his prize like a real treasure. I think a good toy will distract him long enough.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl39: Only a bike path leads to the station, and it's too far to walk. Looks like we'll have to find some suitable transportation.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl40: The trail ahead looks dangerous, and the warning signs aren't exactly reassuring. But it's too late to turn back – we'll have to clear the path and keep going.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl41: Thick fog has completely hidden the road to the artifact. Strangely, the local mushrooms clearly react to water... Maybe they can help us clear this veil.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl42: We found a passage beneath the tree, but the enormous trunk is blocking it completely. We should probably build a machine to remove the tree and open the way.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl43: The artifact is buried under sand. Leo suggests building an amplified guitar and blasting it away with sound. Sometimes I think his ideas are getting crazier...
Data.Epic_Text_lvl44: Marble blocks are scattered all around, and some of them bear curious marks. If we put them together, perhaps we'll finally understand what they were once part of.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl45: Leo insists that all he needs to assemble the artifact is a screen and a curtain. I have no idea how that's supposed to help... but now I'm curious to see it myself.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl46: There's no way we're getting into the museum through the main entrance. We'll have to reach the artifacts from the roof – and we'll definitely need a good grappling hook.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl47: A river separates us from the artifact, and there's no bridge nearby. But there are plenty of beavers around. If we can befriend them, they might help us build a crossing.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl48: A huge rock is completely blocking the way to the artifact. We certainly can't move it, but that local bull looks convincing enough... We just need to make him charge in the right direction.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl50: The sheep have taken over the entire road and seem perfectly comfortable there. If we repair their pen, maybe we can get the flock back where it belongs and clear the way.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl51: This light puzzle is clearly more complicated than it first appeared. We need to restore the mirrors and the obelisk – then perhaps the beams will finally point us toward the answer.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl52: The vineyard owner promised us a valuable artifact in return for our help. I think a little farm work is well worth that reward.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl54: The artifact is stuck high in the branches, and there's no way to climb up there. Looks like we'll need one very accurate shot.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl55: Our investigation has hit another dead end. If there are no new clues among the antiquities, perhaps we should look for them in today's newspapers.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl56_1: The artifact appears to be protected, so we can't simply take it. Maybe if we leave a suitable replacement, no one will notice.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl56_2: We're almost out of time, and the artifact is still keeping its secrets! We need to study it as quickly as possible.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl56_3: It worked! We've studied the artifact, and now I know much more about it. All that's left is to return it to where we found it.
Data.Epic_Text_lvl57: I think we've gathered all the clues. Now we need to arrange them on one board and look at the whole picture – maybe then everything will finally fall into place.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl01: A car blocking the road? No problem! We'll lift it with balloons and move it to the parking lot.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl02: It worked! The tourists rushed to the truck, and we grabbed the Mars slab.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl03: The projector works! The reconstruction is complete, and we found what we needed.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl04: Luck is on our side! We got the excavation permit.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl05: The scarecrow burned, but we managed to save an ancient scroll about Mars!
Data.Comics_Text_lvl07: The soda beat the rust! Inside, we found an old map of the Colosseum.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl08: The model is ready! Now we know where the Colosseum's hidden passages are.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl09: Our trick worked! The door accepted the fake lion and opened.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl10: We did it! The water is draining, and the Colosseum's underground level is safe.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl11: The catapult worked! Goodbye, underground – we're flying to the exit!
Data.Comics_Text_lvl12_1: Oh no! The lift is broken. Maybe these cute goats can help us get down?
Data.Comics_Text_lvl12_2: We found new helpers! The mountain goats will take us straight down.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl13: Can't reach the artifact? Let the wind do all the work for us!
Data.Comics_Text_lvl14: All set! Dynamite – check. Rocks – check. Boom – check. Ancient artifact – check.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl16: The siphon works again! The water rose just as planned, and our find appeared with it.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl17: The statue was too heavy even for us. Luckily, our water friends joined forces and pulled it from the bottom!
Data.Comics_Text_lvl18: Time to forget the dig for a while! Let's turn on the dance machine.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl19: Road blocked! The robot vacuum gets to work and swallows all the debris.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl21: The raccoon fell for the little raccoon doll! Looks like our pass will soon be back with us.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl22: Operation “Save Oleg” is complete! The parrots made a great rescue team and pulled him out of the well.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl25_1: Time to dig! Let's clear the first layer of ash and see what the mountain hid.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl25_2: Nothing under the first layer? Let's dig deeper and clear the next one!
Data.Comics_Text_lvl25_3: Last layer cleared! Looks like we found what we were looking for.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl26: The path is blocked! Time to unleash the battle top and smash through!
Data.Comics_Text_lvl27: The frog goes into the lava! Let's hope the mountain appreciates the gift.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl29: I never thought a watering can would beat smog. But it worked: the air is clear, and the road is visible again!
Data.Comics_Text_lvl30: What a flight! The wind ripped the weeds out by the roots, and the field looks much friendlier now.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl31: Lightning hit the antenna dead on! The weather station is alive, and we have data for the road ahead again.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl34: The flamethrower did its job – burned everything to ashes! Now we just need to reach the altar.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl35: The disguise worked! Dressed as a maid, I got close enough to hear what our rivals wanted to keep secret.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl36: The test worked a little too well… The fake gates crumbled right before our eyes!
Data.Comics_Text_lvl38: Great bait! The kitten is playing, and our lunch is within reach again.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl39: We made it by bike, fixed the antennas, and restored the signal – now we know the way.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl40: Maybe we should've taken the warning signs more seriously. The ground vanished under us, and Leo and I fell somewhere below!
Data.Comics_Text_lvl42: The machine cleared the tree completely... But beneath the roots we found a hidden passage invisible from above.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl43: Leo was right: the music literally blew the sand away. The top of the real Gates of Janus appeared before us!
Data.Comics_Text_lvl44: One strike – and the marble blocks formed the Column of Janus, a magnificent artifact.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl45: I don't know how Leo did it, but behind the screen the fragments somehow became a complete artifact. Sometimes it's better not to ask.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl46: We made it safely down from the roof and finally reached the artifact. Now we can examine it properly.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl47: The beavers are excellent builders! The new bridge is ready, and the river no longer separates us from the artifact.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl48: Leo's plan was crazy, dangerous… and completely effective. The bull smashed the rock as if it were cardboard.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl50: The pen is ready, and the sheep hurried back inside. Clearing a road has never looked this cute.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl51: At last, every mirror sent the light the right way. The beam hit the obelisk, revealing a cache with new coordinates!
Data.Comics_Text_lvl52: The harvest is in, the vineyard owner is happy, and our reward is a new clue – the secret of the Gift of the Golden Dawn.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl54: Perfect shot! The artifact fell from the branch right to us. Almost too easy for a day like this.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl55: The old newspapers gave us the clue we needed: a mention of the mysterious Cup of Liber. The investigation is moving again.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl56_1: The swap went perfectly. The Cup of Liber is ours, a copy is in its place... and nobody seems to have noticed.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl56_2: The research is done, and the Cup is back in its display case. It looks as if nobody ever touched it.
Data.Comics_Text_lvl57: The red lines meet at one point: most of our finds are linked to native Roman gods.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl01_1: Hi! I'm Claire. We have several tasks ahead – let's complete them one by one. Follow the hints, and I'll show you what to do next.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl01_2: Looks like obstacles are blocking the way to our goal. Let's send the archaeologist to clear the path.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl01_3: Hmm, this obstacle isn't so simple. But that won't stop us! Let's see what we can do.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl01_4: Looks like we don't have enough resources to clear the way. No problem! Let's build a food tent first and restock. I'll handle the resources.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl01_5: Congratulations, you're working with me now. Only the scariest part of any expedition remains – paperwork!\nDraw something on the right. Even a dinosaur. I won't tell anyone!
Data.la8_sign_document_2: I hereby join Claire Whitlock's expedition and solemnly promise:
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl02_1: Look, it's a dig site! Nobody knows what's hidden underground, but it could be something very valuable. Let's send the archaeologist and find out!
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl02_2: Perfetto! The excavation revealed a spot for the drone tent. Trust me, they'll become indispensable helpers in our research. Send a worker to build it.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl02_3: Bene! The drone will help us discover what's hidden inside the dig site. Unlike the archaeologist, it ignores obstacles in its path. Select the dig site to investigate it.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl02_4: Benissimo! Now let's order the drone to scan the dig site.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl02_5: Excellent! Now we can find out what's hidden underground. Hover over the dig site.\nThere's an ancient kitchen underground! Build it to gain a new source of food.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl02_6: So that's why the crowd gathered! Let's take a closer look at the artifact.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl03_1: Veil of Mystery: an obstacle, a resource, or something valuable. Let's clear the veil and find out. Click before I change my mind!
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl03_2: Now send in the drone. Let's see what's there.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl07_1: Now we can upgrade the archaeologists' tent! This will increase the number of workers and bring another archaeologist into our team.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl08_1: This is the inventor's tent. Mine, of course! You can craft items and tools here. Click it to see which resources are required.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl12_1: Looks like the lift is broken. To get down, we'll need to repair it first. Let's see what's wrong.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl24_1: Some areas are still unexplored. We don't know what paths, objects, or resources are hidden inside.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl24_2: To reveal unexplored areas, you'll need a map. Pick it up and use it to uncover new territory.
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl36: Now you can use boosters!\nThey provide a temporary bonus and have a cooldown. Use them wisely!
Data.la8_tutorial_lvl46: There are no roads here, and luckily we don't need them. Go wherever you like, explorers. There are still plenty of places no archaeologist has ever set foot!
Data.la8_oleg_screen_2:
You've completed all 10 levels of the demo. The full game has 40 more levels, new locations, puzzles, and more of the story. 

We'd love to know what you enjoyed and what could be improved. Your feedback will help us make the game better.

Want to follow development or talk to the developers about the game?
